analysis.title: What's Top of Mind in Macro Research: AI jitters, global elections, commodity diversification
key_insights: AI capex funding and returns concerns have pressured AI-related equities and widened credit spreads on related corporate debt. GS Risk Appetite Indicator is negative for the first time since March and the Sentiment and Positioning Indicator is at its lowest since April.
GS expects solid earnings, lighter positioning and lower valuations to support equities into year-end, and sees scope for further near-term reversal of the recent selloff in USD HY.

GS equity analysts upgraded CoreWeave to Buy (from Neutral) on an expected favorable ROIC/WACC spread, even with a higher cost of debt, as new contract datapoints emerge over the next 12 months. Neocloud issuers have been the center of the equity and credit stress.

GS recommends diversified equity exposures, with US consumer-facing laggards attractive as real income growth is expected to improve next year. Credit dispersion across AI-related issuers will stay elevated.

GS sees a stronger case for bond allocations because recent AI-related equity and credit weakness showed bonds act as a hedge to the AI theme, even though Treasuries have been a poor hedge to the broad equity market.

Prediction markets assign high odds to a Democratic sweep in the US midterms. GS does not expect that outcome to meaningfully change policy toward the Iran war or AI regulation. Reduced political uncertainty could support equities, but inflation, earnings and geopolitics matter more.
Brazil's presidential runoff is on October 25. A market-friendly outcome would likely support further gains in Brazilian equities, but sustaining a rally would require concrete policy action.

Israel holds legislative elections on October 27. Any post-election shekel strength is unlikely to last, and GS would use it as an entry point to re-engage ILS shorts, which screen as a hedge for portfolios levered to tech stocks.
Spain's snap election on November 29 could support a re-rating of Spanish sovereign debt if it yields a clear majority able to pass a budget.

In France a budget now looks likely before year-end, but Marine Le Pen's proposed fiscal framework leaves France on a challenging path. GS now forecasts 10y OAT-Bund spreads of 130bp by mid-2027 and 100bp by end-2027 (from 95bp and 80bp).

GS keeps a positive commodities allocation, both tactically and structurally. It sees Middle East energy supply adapting to the conflict and eventually lowering oil and gas prices, but still sees upside risks, with Brent above $105/bbl and European gas above €86/MWh.
GS expects copper to keep rising as US-China competition tightens the ex-US market, and raised its end-2026/average 2027 forecasts to $14,700/$15,400 per tonne (from $13,735/$13,800).

US housing starts fell significantly in September. GS expects more supply and homebuilder margins compressing to pre-pandemic levels to weigh on single-family starts (0.87mn in 2027 vs 0.90mn in 2026) and demand to stay tepid on affordability.
GS forecasts residential fixed investment growth declining through 2H27 (-2.5%/-4%/-1% annualized in 4Q26/1Q27/2Q27).
